title: CLAUDE.md
text: R package mass spectrometry-based label-free quantification (LFQ) proteomics analysis. provides complete workflow: QC, normalization, protein aggregation, statistical modelling, hypothesis testing, sample size estimation. Data always long (tidy) format. Branch Modelling2R6 active development branch.

title: CLAUDE.md
code: Raw Data + AnalysisConfiguration → LFQData     ├── get_Transformer() → LFQDataTransformer  (log2, robscale, normalize)     ├── get_Aggregator()  → LFQDataAggregator   (peptide → protein rollup)     ├── get_Stats()       → LFQDataStats         (CV, variance per group)     ├── get_Plotter()     → LFQDataPlotter       (heatmaps, PCA, boxplots)     ├── get_Summariser()  → LFQDataSummariser    (missingness, hierarchy counts)     └── get_Imputer()     → LFQDataImp           (missing value imputation)  LFQData → build_model(strategy) → Model     └── Contrasts$new(model, contrast_spec) → contrast results         ├── ContrastsModerated  (prolfqua squeezeVarRob shrinkage)         ├── ContrastsProDA      (missing-data-aware)         ├── ContrastsMissing    (imputation-based)         ├── ContrastsFirth      (Firth logistic)         └── get_Plotter() → ContrastsPlotter (volcano, MA, heatmap)  LFQData → build_model_limma(strategy_limma) → ModelLimma     └── ContrastsLimma$new(model, contrast_spec) → contrast results         └── Same downstream API: get_contrasts(), get_Plotter(), to_wide()

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Decorator/Composition: LFQData factory methods (get_Transformer(), get_Plotter(), etc.) return decorator objects wrap LFQData. Decorators hold reference lfq field. Method chaining: Transformer methods return self chaining, access result via $lfq: Strategy pattern models: strategy_lm(), strategy_lmer(), strategy_rlm(), strategy_glm() return lists model_fun, contrast_fun, isSingular, anova_df. strategy_limma() returns simpler list (formula, trend, robust) consumed build_model_limma(). Config immutability: AnalysisConfiguration always deep-cloned passed new LFQData instances. Never modify config -place existing LFQData.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Flat R6 class maps column roles data: - hierarchy: ordered measurement levels (protein_Id → peptide_Id → precursor_Id → fragment_Id). hierarchyDepth controls level modelled. - factors: explanatory variables (group, treatment). factorDepth controls interaction depth. - workIntensity: response column. Uses stack (set_response() / pop_response() / get_response()) working multiple intensity columns. - fileName: sample identifier column. Concrete config factories: create_config_MQ_peptide(), create_config_Skyline(), create_config_Spectronaut_Peptide(), etc. tidyMS_R6_ConcreteConfigurations.R.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: setup_analysis(data, config) — prepare data analysis (AnalysisConfiguration.R) build_model(data, strategy, subject_Id) — fit per-protein models (tidyMS_R6Model.R) build_model_limma(lfqdata, strategy) — fit limma matrix model (ContrastsLimma.R) strategy_lm(), strategy_lmer(), strategy_rlm(), strategy_glm() — per-protein model strategies (tidyMS_R6_Modelling.R) strategy_limma() — limma matrix model strategy (ContrastsLimma.R) sim_lfq_data_peptide_config() — simulate test data (simulate_LFQ_data.R)

title: CLAUDE.md
text: R/LFQData*.R — Core data container decorator classes R/Model*.R, R/Contrasts*.R — Modelling hypothesis testing R/AnalysisConfiguration.R — Configuration system R/tidyMS_R6_*.R — Model strategies, concrete configs, correlation analysis R/tidyMS_*.R — Utility functions (plotting, stats, aggregation, missingness)

text: 7 test files tests/testthat/: - test-LFQData.R — Core data container decorators - test-Model.R — Model fitting coefficient extraction - test-Contrasts.R — Contrast computation - test-ContrastsLimma.R — Limma backend (ModelLimma, ContrastsLimma, merge, 2-factor) - test-ContrastsPlotter.R — Contrast visualization - test-plotting_functions.R — Low-level plots - test-tidyconfig_functions.R — Configuration utilities

title: DEqMS-style Count-Dependent Variance Moderation
text: vignette demonstrates ContrastsModeratedDEqMS, count-dependent variance shrinkage method inspired DEqMS approach (Zhu et al., 2020). drop-alternative ContrastsModerated: ContrastsModerated (standard): applies single global prior variance proteins — every protein shrunk toward value. ContrastsModeratedDEqMS (count-dependent): prior variance depends number peptides/PSMs used quantify protein. Proteins quantified many peptides get less shrinkage (variance already well estimated); proteins peptides get . matters proteomics quantification depth varies hugely across proteins. protein quantified 20 peptides much better-estimated variance one 2 peptides, receive prior. user-facing API identical ContrastsModerated: downstream methods (get_contrasts, get_Plotter, to_wide, merge_contrasts_results).

title: DEqMS-style Count-Dependent Variance Moderation
text: Fit LOESS: log(sigma^2) ~ log2(peptide_count) — captures count-dependent variance trend. Estimate prior df (d0): residual variance around LOESS curve, using trigammaInverse approach (math limma/squeezeVarRob). Count-specific prior variance: s0^2(count) varies per protein, derived fitted LOESS curve. Posterior variance: Bayesian shrinkage combining observed prior: var.post = (d0 * s0^2(count) + df * sigma^2) / (d0 + df) Moderated t-statistics p-values recomputed posterior variance.

title: Limma Backend for prolfqua
text: vignette demonstrates limma backend prolfqua’s modelling pipeline. limma backend drop-alternative per-protein lm + squeezeVar pipeline. approaches fit linear models perform empirical Bayes variance shrinkage, : prolfqua default (strategy_lm + Contrasts + ContrastsModerated): fits one lm() per protein, applies prolfqua’s squeezeVarRob moderation. limma backend (strategy_limma + ContrastsLimma): uses limma’s matrix-based lmFit + contrasts.fit + eBayes pipeline directly. user-facing API identical: formula specification, contrast specification, downstream methods (get_contrasts, get_Plotter, to_wide, merge_contrasts_results).

packageVersion("prolfqua")  ## here we simulate peptide level data startdata <- sim_lfq_data_peptide_config() lfqpep <- LFQData$new(startdata$data, startdata$config)   ## transform intensities lfqpep <- lfqpep$get_Transformer()$log2()$robscale()$lfq lfqpep$rename_response("log_peptide_abundance") agr <- lfqpep$get_Aggregator() lfqpro <- agr$medpolish() lfqpro$rename_response("log_protein_abundance")  ## plot Figure 3 panels A-D pl <- lfqpep$get_Plotter() panelA <- pl$intensity_distribution_density() +   ggplot2::labs(tag = "A") + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none") panelB <- agr$plot()$plots[[1]] + ggplot2::labs(tag = "B") panelC <- lfqpro$get_Stats()$violin() + ggplot2::labs(tag = "C") pl <- lfqpro$get_Plotter() panelD <- pl$boxplots()$boxplot[[1]] + ggplot2::labs(tag = "D") ggpubr::ggarrange(panelA, panelB, panelC, panelD) ## specify model modelFunction <-  strategy_lm("log_protein_abundance  ~ group_")  ## fit models to lfqpro data mod <- build_model(  lfqpro,  modelFunction )  ## specify contrasts Contr <- c("AvsCtrl" = "group_A - group_Ctrl",      "BvsCtrl" = "group_B - group_Ctrl",      "BvsA" = "group_B - group_A"       )        ## determine contrasts and plot contrastX <- prolfqua::Contrasts$new(mod, Contr) pl <- contrastX$get_Plotter() pl$volcano()$FDR
